title: Convergence of averaged Gaussian indicators
statement: Let $n\ge0$ and let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable. If $u_\theta(x)=\int 1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$, then $\int |u_\theta(x)-1_A(x)|\,d\gamma_n(x)\to0$ as the real parameter $\theta$ tends to $0$.
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. If $A$ is measurable, then $\int|u_\theta-1_A|\,d\gamma_n\to0$ as $\theta\to0$ through real values.
